key_insight: AgentBeats proposes Agentified Agent Assessment (AAA), a unified judge-agent framework that standardizes agent evaluation through A2A and MCP interfaces instead of benchmark-specific harnesses.
engineering_relevance: The framework is relevant for building fair, interoperable, and reproducible evaluation pipelines for diverse AI agents, especially in multi-agent and tool-using systems.
method: Define AAA with judge agents as evaluators and standardized A2A/MCP protocols for all participants.
Introduce AgentBeats as a concrete implementation with five operation modes to fit openness, privacy, and reproducibility constraints.
Validate the framework through a large open competition and a coding-agent case study.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports a five-month open competition with 298 judge agents across 12 categories and 467 subject agents, plus a coding-agent case study that preserved public-record fidelity while revealing missing head-to-head results.
watch_item: Standardized judge-agent evaluation may still depend on careful protocol design and governance to avoid bias, privacy leakage, or inconsistent assessments across benchmarks.
paper_title: AgentBeats: Agentifying Agent Assessment for Openness, Standardization, and Reproducibility
